name: South Face Center

days.note: Approach as for the standard South Face to the Concord-Lexington col, then aid/free the obvious center crack of the south face for two pitches before joining the North Face route's final pitch to reach the summit. The A3 pitches are notably slower going than the free lines nearby.
days.title: Car-to-car: South Face Center
days.objective: Climb South Face Center (5.7 A3) finishing via the North Face's last pitch

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day (about 10 hrs car-to-car) — this is the slowest of Concord's rock lines because of the aid climbing on the two center-crack pitches.

overview: A shorter, steeper variation up the center of Concord's south face, starting about 100 ft climber's-left (west) of the standard South Face line. Historically climbed with a short bit of aid (5.7 A3) before being freed at its current, harder free grade; the route finishes by joining the upper portion of the North Face route to the summit.
watch_out: thin/marginal gear on the aid-derived sections
route-finding to stay on-line and correctly join the North Face finish
loose rock in the approach gully
pro_tips: Expect thin, sometimes marginal protection on sections that were originally climbed with aid (5.7 A3).
